text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn stressed connections between German and European reunion in a festive speech he delivered at the celebrations in Munich yesterday marking the anniversary of Germany's reunification. @

- Reports completed by the Supervisory Board of the State Privatisation and Holding Co (APV) and the Governmental Supervisory Office prepared for today's cabinet meeting question the legality of contracts concluded by the APV and a lawyer, and have revealed a number of facts that could have legal and personal consequences.
- The Romanian house of deputies approved the Romanian-Hungarian basic treaty on Thursday. @
- Agriculture Minister Laszlo Lakos expects increasing yields, better competitiveness and 'reasonable' increase in the price of foodstuffs for next year.
- The Hungarian Investment and Development Bank and Konzumbank will each have a 25 percent stake in the new Cetelem bank to be opened here next year.
- Police have arrested 14 suspects, including seven border guards and one customs guard, for smuggling stolen cars to Romania. @
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The cabinet today is expected to discuss the transformation of the social insurance contribution system and consider guidelines for transforming agriculture subsidies.
- The EU's Council of Transport Ministers agreed yesterday to start negotiations towards the conclusion of bilateral aviation agreements with associated member states.

- In an address to the UN General Assembly yesterday, Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs stressed the need to increase the world body's potential to prevent crimes and manage crises, and the importance of defending minority and human rights. @

- The gas firm Tigaz, the majority of which is owned by Italgas, has offered to buy the gas pipelines from local governments in Szabolcs-Szatmar county. The firm would acquire the entire network for 40 percent of its HUF 10 billion value.
- The football stadium and other properties of entrepreneur Jozsef Stadler will be auctioned off on October 25.
- The national telecom company Matav connected its 2,000,000th telephone line yesterday. @
NEPSZABADSAG
- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze Thursday confirmed that alleged fraudster Gyorgy Zemplenyi cannot be extradited to foreign authorities under the Hungarian Penal Code.
- The number of registered unemployed increased by 6,200 to 501,000 last month, bringing the nationwide rate to 11 percent.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Sandor Lezsak, head of the Democratic Forum, said Thursday he expected a heavy turnout for Saturday afternoon's demonstration outside Parliament. @
- MPs' present gross monthly salary of 87,750 forints is expected to be raised to 100,913 forints from January 1997.
- The road show to promote an 11.7 percent stake in BorsodChem Rt to West European and Hungarian investors begins today.
- The employees of the national telecommunication firm Matav bought up all the 278,800 shares offered to them during the subscription period that ended on Wednesday.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
